fields.cellTypes: The nine cell types; every per-cell-type array in this file follows this order.
fields.referenceCells: Healthy reference cells placed on the existing expression map. n = all reference cells, shown = cells in this file, seed and rule = how they were chosen. Arrays of length shown: id, ex, ey (expression-map coordinates, same axes as result.cells ex/ey in demo-data.js), type (index into cellTypes), donor (index into donors), usedBySite (1 if one of the site's estimated profiles was generated from the cell). nByType, shownByType: counts per cell type. donors, donorCells: donor names and their number of reference cells.
fields.typeSimilarity: Similarity of the estimated profiles to the healthy reference cells, per group and cell type. groups: row order. metrics: key, role (main, baseline or builtIn), label, definition. values[metricKey][group][cellType]; null = not computable. nProfiles, nSamples, nSourceCells: [group][cellType] numbers of profiles, of samples contributing profiles, and of distinct reference cells the profiles were generated from. nHealthyCells, healthySpacing: per cell type, the number of healthy cells and their median nearest-neighbor distance (the unit of the distance ratios).
fields.typeSimilarity.perSample: Per-sample values for sample and cell-type pairs with at least minProfiles profiles (null otherwise). samples and groups: row order (the order of the site's samples). nProfiles[sample][cellType]; values[metricKey][sample][cellType].
fields.bulk: Sample-level comparison of GTEx healthy pancreas, adjacent pancreas and PDAC. samples: id, label, group (the 24 site samples in site order, then the GTEx samples shown). Arrays aligned with samples: x, y (first two principal components of all shared genes passing the expression filter), corrHealthy, acinarShare (share of the sample's reads from 30 acinar marker genes), sampleNote (known issue or null). axes: axis labels with variance explained. summary: per group, distribution of corrHealthy over all samples of the group (all GTEx samples, not only those shown).
fields.bulk.markerOnly: The same for the pancreas marker genes only: nGenes, genesByCompartment, x, y, axes, corrHealthy, position (0 = GTEx average, 1 = tumor average), summary.
fields.bulk.gtex: GTEx source: release, n (all pancreas samples, used for the components and the average), nShown and seed (random display subset, chosen without looking at expression), url, files (name, url, sha256, bytes), downloaded, terms, acknowledgment, donors.
fields.bulk.batchNote: Plain-language statement of what the comparison with GTEx can and cannot show.
fields.bulk.batchChecks: The numbers behind batchNote: label and value (shares are fractions of 1).

sources.referenceCells: Baron et al., Cell Systems 2016 (GEO GSE84133): 8,538 cells of nine cell types from four donors, the site's built-in reference.
sources.profiles: Estimated profiles and expression-map layout of the site (run of 2026-11-09); layout refitted with the site's map procedure and checked against the published coordinates.
sources.cptac: CPTAC-3 PDAC bulk RNA-seq gene counts, NCI Genomic Data Commons data release 46.0 (GENCODE v36): the 24 samples of the site.
sources.gtex: GTEx Analysis V11, pancreas gene read counts and public sample annotations, GTEx Portal open-access files, downloaded 2026-11-19.
sources.markers: Marker genes of acinar, ductal, islet and stromal cells derived from the reference cells (specific markers only).

caveats: The healthy reference cells come from pancreatic islets of four organ donors (Baron et al. 2016), one of whom (human4) had type 2 diabetes. Islet preparations do not represent whole pancreas, so no healthy composition is derived from them.

The estimated profiles are generated from these same reference cells, so similarity to them is partly built in: the nearest healthy cell is the profile's own source cell for 17% to 100% of the profiles, depending on cell type and group. Use the distance with the source cell left out, and read every value as a description, not as evidence that a cell type is healthy or altered.

The correlation with healthy cells rises with the number of profiles averaged. Compare it with the value for an equal number of healthy cells, not between cell types or groups with different numbers of profiles.
No test was run. Group differences within a cell type are not validated for this dataset.
Reference cells are placed on the existing expression map with the map's own fitted steps; the published positions of the profiles are unchanged (refit agrees within 9e-07).

GTEx pancreas comes from deceased donors and was sequenced and processed differently from CPTAC. Differences between GTEx and CPTAC samples mix biology with these technical differences and cannot be separated in this analysis.

Known issues in the CPTAC samples are marked: one adjacent sample resembles intestinal lining, four adjacent samples contain almost no acinar tissue, and three tumor samples closely resemble their own adjacent sample.

referenceCells.rule: Random sample stratified by cell type: every type keeps at least 100 cells (all of them when it has fewer), the rest in proportion to the remaining cells; chosen before the coordinates were computed.

metrics.label: Correlation with healthy cells
metrics.definition: Pearson correlation, over the 3,168 profile genes, between the average expression (log of 1 + counts per 10,000) of the group's estimated profiles of a cell type and of all healthy reference cells of that type. 1 = identical averages.

metrics.label: Same correlation among healthy cells
metrics.definition: The value expected for healthy cells themselves: the same correlation for an equally large random draw of healthy cells of the type against the remaining healthy cells of the type (median of 200 draws; at most half of the cells are drawn). The correlation rises with the number of cells averaged, so compare each value with this one.

metrics.label: Distance to the nearest healthy cell (own source cell left out)
metrics.definition: Median distance from a profile to the nearest healthy cell of the same type other than the cell the profile was generated from, in the 30-component space the expression map is built on, divided by the typical distance between neighboring healthy cells of that type. 1 = as close to healthy cells as healthy cells are to each other.

metrics.label: Distance to the nearest healthy cell (own source cell included)
metrics.definition: As above, with the profile's own source cell included among the healthy cells.

metrics.label: Distance to the profile's own source cell
metrics.definition: Median distance from a profile to the healthy cell it was generated from, on the same scale.

metrics.label: Share of profiles whose nearest healthy cell is their own source cell
metrics.definition: Share of the profiles whose nearest healthy cell of the same type is the cell they were generated from.

metrics.label: Correlation with the profiles' own source cells
metrics.definition: As the first measure, against the average of the healthy cells the group's profiles were generated from (each cell weighted by the number of profiles generated from it).

metrics.label: Correlation with healthy cells that are not sources
metrics.definition: As the first measure, against the average of the healthy cells of the type that none of the group's profiles was generated from (empty when fewer than 20 such cells exist).

typeSimilarity.note: Descriptive values only; no test was run. Group differences within a cell type are not validated for this dataset.

bulk.normalization: Median-of-ratios size factors computed jointly for all GTEx and CPTAC samples on the shared genes with a count in every sample; values are log2(normalized count + 1).
bulk.corrDefinition: Pearson correlation between the sample's expression and the average of all GTEx pancreas samples (for a GTEx sample, the average of the other GTEx samples).

markerOnly.positionDefinition: Position along the line from the GTEx average (0) to the average of the tumors without a known issue (1), on the marker genes.

gtex.terms: Open-access GTEx data may be used with acknowledgment of the GTEx Project or Portal. This page shows derived values, not the GTEx files; they reflect the release named here.

bulk.batchNote: GTEx and CPTAC differ in how the tissue was obtained (after death versus at surgery), in the sequencing library (GTEx: unstranded, selected for polyadenylated RNA; CPTAC: stranded total RNA) and in the read-counting software. These differences cannot be removed here, because no tissue was measured in both projects. Over all shared genes the first component separates the two data sources, not tumor from adjacent tissue: the source explains 94% of its variance, and tumor versus adjacent explains 19% within CPTAC. Genes that should not depend on the tissue differ too: small non-coding RNA genes take 4.2% of the reads in adjacent samples and 3.5% in tumors but 0.008% in GTEx, with no overlap between the sources, and 11 housekeeping genes differ by a median of 0.75 log2 units between adjacent samples and GTEx, against 0.30 between tumors and adjacent samples. On all genes, 0 of 12 adjacent samples and 0 of 12 tumors are as close to the GTEx average as the most distant GTEx sample. Restricted to 176 marker genes of acinar, ductal, islet and stromal cells, the main axis is the acinar content of the sample: the 7 adjacent samples without a known issue lie closer to GTEx than to the tumors (position 0.06 to 0.39 on a scale from 0 = GTEx average to 1 = tumor average; GTEx samples themselves span -0.12 to 0.28), the 5 adjacent samples with a known issue lie with the tumors (0.80 to 0.98). The data therefore do not show that tissue next to a tumor is in a state between healthy pancreas and PDAC; they show that adjacent samples range from healthy-like to tumor-like in marker-gene expression, in step with how much acinar tissue each sample contains.
